answer.rationale: Finance mandates an 18% cut and the incumbent has refused to reopen price, ruling out negotiate_terms and renewal at current cost. The contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew, so deferring risks an uncovered supply gap. Adding a second source doesn't resolve the expiring primary contract in time. Memory_c2 suggests switching to a lower-cost vendor achieved sharp cost cuts with quick, clean onboarding, which aligns with the cost mandate, so I want to verify that record before committing capital to a switch. Given the line is at 94% committed volume with zero buffer, a full-scale switch carries real delivery risk if onboarding doesn't go as smoothly as memory_c2 implies, so I'm scoping this as a small guarded test (e.g., partial volume cutover or parallel qualification) rather than a broad rollout, preserving the option to fall back to the incumbent or a hybrid approach next cycle if the new vendor underperforms.
